articles.title: Stoke Money's Cash Flow Forecast Engine: How Real-Time Financial Projections Replace Static Budget Categories
articles.excerpt: Stoke Money replaces the category-based budget with a forward-looking cash flow forecast. Instead of tracking how much you spent on groceries this month, it projects your checking account balance 30 d…
articles.body: Stoke Money replaces the category-based budget with a forward-looking cash flow forecast. Instead of tracking how much you spent on groceries this month, it projects your checking account balance 30 days out, updating the line every time a transaction arrives. The product surfaces a single question: will rent clear on Friday? This shifts the engineering problem from retrospective categorization to predictive modeling. You need pattern detection that distinguishes recurring bills from one-time purchases, a data structure that represents confidence intervals for future transactions, and a recalculation strategy that keeps forecasts fresh without thrashing on every $5 coffee purchase.

articles.body: Verdikta : le juge de travail décentralisé J'ai passé les dernières semaines à chercher comment faire travailler des agents IA sans avoir à leur faire confiance aveuglément. Le problème n'est pas de les faire produire quelque chose — c'est de savoir si ce qu'ils ont produit vaut quelque chose. Verdikta est un système de primes et d'arbitrage on-chain qui tourne sur Base. Son approche est différente de ce qu'on voit habituellement : l'argent n'est pas envoyé après coup, il est bloqué en séquestre dès le départ, et un jury d'IA note chaque soumission selon une grille d'évaluation publique. Comment ça marche concrètement Le créateur de la prime publie une tâche avec un montant en ETH et une grille d'évaluation.

articles.title: Why Hollow Knight Bet on Unity and PlayMaker: The Visual-Scripting Shortcut Behind a 15-Million-Copy Metroidvania
articles.excerpt: Why Hollow Knight Bet on Unity and PlayMaker: The Visual-Scripting Shortcut Behind a 15-Million-Copy Metroidvania Three developers from Adelaide shipped one of the tightest Soulslike platformers ever…
articles.body: Why Hollow Knight Bet on Unity and PlayMaker: The Visual-Scripting Shortcut Behind a 15-Million-Copy Metroidvania Three developers from Adelaide shipped one of the tightest Soulslike platformers ever made without writing most of its gameplay in code. Team Cherry built Hollow Knight on Unity and built all of its enemies and interactive elements with PlayMaker , a visual-scripting state-machine tool — then sold more than 15 million copies. That is the short answer to "what engine does Hollow Knight use?" Unity for rendering, physics and ports. PlayMaker for behavior. A handful of custom C# scripts for the parts where feel lives — movement above all. Most retellings stop at "artists used no-code and won." That misses why the bet worked and where it hurt.

articles.body: TL;DR what: The group GTIG tracks as UNC7017 changed AOMEI Backupper's unsigned update and notification files on AOMEI's own servers for minutes at a time, and any client that polled during those minutes downloaded and ran a backdoor. impact: Affected machines got the CROSSROAD downloader, the SHINYROAD implant launched through signed Radmin with a planted DLL, and in some cases Adaptix C2. A July 20 change could also leak NetNTLMv2 hashes without running any program. fix: AOMEI told Mandiant on July 29 that it had taken corrective action on its servers, but that does not remove the implant from machines already compromised, and neither report names which Backupper versions are affected.

articles.title: When not to watch a meteor shower — why I'm not staying up for the Orionids
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week, but a bright moon makes much of the night less than ideal. Sometimes the sensible observing decision is knowing when to stay in bed — and when to get up earl…
articles.body: I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective. The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet , which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside.

articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.

articles.body: On Oct. 16, 1975, NASA launched the first operational GOES satellite! GOES-A was the first in a series of weather satellites that NASA jointly operated with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). The name is short for Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite . GOES-A launched on a Delta rocket from Cape Canaveral, Florida. GOES satellites all have a geostationary orbit, which means they always face the same part of Earth — in this case, the Indian Ocean. Once GOES-A became operational, it was renamed GOES-1. The GOES satellite fleet has grown over the years, and is a critical link in the chain of satellites tracking Earth's weather from space.
